rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Servers and networking equipment': 172.492B − 113.156B = 59.336B, or 45% of 131.819B capex. This counts all server and network growth, including non-AI AWS and retail compute, and it is net of retirements. It excludes datacenter shells (Land and buildings +32.1B) and construction in progress (+25.1B). The company says the capex increase 'primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence' but gives no amount.

Growth in gross 'Equipment': 218.893B − 185.039B = 33.854B, or 41% of 82.999B capex. Before FY2025, Amazon reported a single Equipment category, which bundles servers and networking with heavy (fulfillment) and other equipment; its FY2024 balance equals the sum of the three FY2025 subcategories. The figure therefore overstates server growth, includes non-AI servers, and is net of retirements.

Growth in gross 'Equipment': 185.039B − 157.458B = 27.581B, or 52% of 52.729B capex. The category includes fulfillment and other equipment as well as servers, and the pack has no AI statement for this year. This is an upper bound on server growth, not an AI amount.

Growth in gross 'Equipment': 157.458B − 128.683B = 28.775B, or 45% of 63.645B capex. The category includes fulfillment and other equipment as well as servers, and FY2022 predates the generative-AI buildout with no AI statement in the pack. Read this as general equipment growth, not AI.

Amazon expects 'about $200 billion in capital expenditures across Amazon in 2026', citing AI, chips, robotics and low earth orbit satellites. That figure is total capex, not the AI part, and no AI share or amount is given.

The MD&A says spending in technology and infrastructure will increase as Amazon adds infrastructure and employees, 'including to support our artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives'. No amount or share is given.
